subject: Learning Methods
title: The Feeling of Knowing
description: Learn The Feeling of Knowing in one minute.

hook.text: It is on the tip of your tongue. You feel certain you know it but cannot retrieve it. That feeling has a name.

buildup.text: The feeling of knowing is a metacognitive judgment. Your brain estimates retrieval likelihood before trying.

discovery.text: Research shows this feeling is often accurate but not always. Familiarity can trick you into false confidence.

twist.text: Re-reading notes creates strong familiarity. You feel you know it. But recognition is not the same as recall.

climax.text: Test yourself instead of checking if material looks familiar. Recall reveals true knowledge; recognition hides gaps.

punchline.text: Feeling you know is not knowing. Test yourself.

quiz.question: Why is the feeling of knowing sometimes misleading?
options: It only works for visual information
Familiarity from re-reading creates false confidence
